rounds.q: Add up every dot on a regular six-sided die. What's the total?
rounds.why: Opposite faces always add up to 7: 1 and 6, 2 and 5, 3 and 4.
rounds.src: Cut the Knot (A. Bogomolny), Two Dice (standard die faces 1 to 6)
rounds.fun: Three pairs that each make 7. That's 21 dots of pure luck!

rounds.q: Roll two dice. What % of the time do they add up to 7?
rounds.why: 6 of the 36 possible rolls make 7 (16.7%), but only 1 in 36 makes snake eyes.
rounds.src: OpenIntro Statistics, Table 2.5: sum of two dice (LibreTexts)
rounds.fun: Lucky 7 shows up 6 ways out of 36. Snake eyes only has 1. Poor snake!

rounds.q: What year did a computer first beat the world chess champion in a match?
rounds.why: The winning computer could check 200 million chess positions every second.
rounds.src: IBM, Deep Blue history page (1997 match)
rounds.fun: 200 million chess positions a second. No wonder it never needed a snack break!

rounds.q: How old is the average US video game player?
rounds.why: About 212.3 million Americans play video games.
rounds.src: Entertainment Software Association, Essential Facts (2026 report)
rounds.fun: The average player is 37. Grown-ups love a good button mash too!

rounds.q: How many tiles are in a standard double-six domino set?
rounds.why: Go up to double-twelve and the set jumps to 91 tiles.
rounds.fun: 28 tiles for double-six, 91 for double-twelve. That's a long game night!
